subject: Acme - Post-call pricing & context-length follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - Post-call pricing & context-length follow-up

Hi Sarah / Tom  great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from todays discovery: 

1) Usage profile (high level): Sarah mentioned ~2M user interactions/month for the help widget pilot, with a long-tail of heavy users. We need to nail unit economics before pilot.
2) Context & output sizing: initial expectation is avg prompt ~320 tokens, avg completion ~380 tokens for the widget; however they expect occasional long-doc workflows (document summarization + Q&A) that could require 32k context and rare archival/transfer cases that might need 128k.
3) Primary asks from Acme: target cost per 1M tokens (budget sweet spot), and conservative pricing for 8k vs 32k vs 128k contexts so they can size the pilot budget.

Attached: a short context profiling worksheet (2026-07-22_acme_context_profile.csv) that I filled with the numbers you shared on the call, and a rough pricing estimate template (redwood_pricing_estimate_1M_tokens.xlsx).

Next steps I propose: 
- You (Acme) confirm monthly token volume bands (low/expected/high) for both widget and long-doc flows by EOD Friday (7/24).
- We provide a short MLP pricing table (8k/32k/128k rows) + example unit economics for $/1M tokens and expected monthly cost by Monday.
- Align on procurement timeline  Tom can loop procurement when we have a budget band.

Thanks  Ill draft the short pricing table and send over.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmecorp.com>

Cc: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call pricing & context-length follow-up

Thanks Marissa  useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Monthly token bands: low ~50M, expected ~250M, high 600M (these are total tokens: prompt+completion). The widget will be ~70% of volume, long-doc flows ~25%, and the rest experimental.
- Avg sizes (from sampling): widget prompt ~300 tokens / completion ~400 tokens. Long-doc queries average prompt 2,500 tokens with completions around 900 tokens (the summarization + Q&A flow).
- 8k context covers ~95% of widget and some long-doc Q&A; 32k will be required for full-document summarization use cases and iterative sessions (~15% of long-doc flows). 128k is rare  maybe 12% for huge legal docs during post-MVP tests.

Procurement (cc) asked: what is the expected list price per 1M tokens for each context tier? Well use that to validate budget with finance.

Sarah
Product Manager, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmecorp.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call pricing & context-length follow-up

Thanks for the detail, Sarah  super helpful. A couple of quick notes as I prep the pricing table: 

- Given your bands (50M / 250M / 600M total tokens), well model economics both on a hostered per-token price and a Dedicated reserved-option for the expected/high tiers (since Dedicated can materially lower $/1M at scale).
- For the pricing table Ill show: (a) list per-1M-token price by context tier (8k/32k/128k), (b) expected monthly cost at low/expected/high, (c) effective $/1M after volume discounts and caching/kv savings assumptions.
- Questions for you: do you have a target budget number or target $/1M token (ballpark) that Finance would accept? If you give a target, we can show configurations that hit it.

Jordan (cc)  can you add the quick notes on how we normalize tokens for the long-doc summarization flows (prompt vs completion split and streaming considerations)?

-Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call pricing & context-length follow-up

Quick notes from infra/SE perspective: 

- Token accounting: we bill prompt + completion tokens. For the long-doc summarization (2,500 prompt / 900 completion avg) well treat the prompt as split across streaming chunks when applicable; caching on repeated doc queries reduces prompt cost on follow-ups.

- Typical effective unit economics: with intelligent batching, prefix caching and KV cache hit assumptions (well assume 2030% prompt token savings on repeated docs) the effective $/1M for 8k contexts is substantially lower than for 32k/128k because of kernel choices and memory overhead.

- Practical guidance for pricing table: assume three tiers: 8k (default), 32k (extended), 128k (archival/rare). For modeling I suggest base list prices be shown, then an example effective price after 10%/20%/35% volumetric discounts. Ill attach a short note to the pricing sheet.

- Also note: Dedicated reserved capacity can reduce cost by ~3045% depending on commit and utilization  good to show as a second column.

-Jordan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

If you can send that by EOD Monday, we can route to Finance and come back with a preferred band. Also please include any estimated onboarding credits or pilot discounts for PoC.
